title: No dig, no nslookup, and getent only answers A/AAAA
claim: Slim agent containers ship without dig, nslookup, and host; getent is the only resolver available, and because it queries only A/AAAA records, empty output does not mean the domain is unregistered.
appliesTo: Slim containers built without bind-utils, common in agent and CI images.
expectation: Standard DNS debugging tools are present, or their absence is obvious enough to route around quickly.
reality: `command -v dig nslookup host` returns nothing at all, and dig invocations silently produce empty output rather than a not-found error — which looks exactly like an NXDOMAIN. `getent hosts` works, but resolves only address records, so a domain with NS and MX but no A record returns nothing.
mechanism: getent goes through NSS, not a DNS client, so it is limited to the host-lookup path. It has no concept of record types beyond addresses.
workaround: Use `getent hosts <domain>` for liveness, and state the limit when reporting: 'no A record' is the honest claim, 'the domain is unregistered' is not. For anything beyond address records, use DNS-over-HTTPS against an allowlisted resolver, or say the check was not possible.

evidence.command: command -v dig nslookup host; for t in A NS CNAME; do dig +short $t example.invalid; done
evidence.output:
(no output from command -v)
(no output from any dig invocation)
evidence.note: The empty dig output is the trap: it is absence of the binary, not absence of the record.
getent does work, which makes the silent dig failure easier to miss.

check.command: command -v dig nslookup host || echo ABSENT; getent hosts example.com >/dev/null && echo GETENT_OK
check.confirmedIf: ABSENT is printed and GETENT_OK is printed
check.refutedIf: any of dig, nslookup, or host resolves to a path

observations.note: Nearly reported a domain as unregistered on the strength of empty getent output.
